blocks.content: This topic goes deeper into parallelism, covering the two distinct patterns Jobs support for running multiple Pods concurrently, and when each one actually fits.
1. Multiple Pods, Working at the Same Time
blocks.text: 1. Multiple Pods, Working at the Same Time

blocks.content: Setting parallelism above 1 means several Pods for the same Job run concurrently, rather than the Job working through its completions one Pod at a time, sequentially.

blocks.alt: Several Pods genuinely working at the same time, not one after another

blocks.content: The most common pattern combines completions and parallelism together, completions: 10, parallelism: 3 means 10 total successful runs are needed, with up to 3 running concurrently at any given moment, working through the total in batches.

blocks.alt: A known total, worked through in concurrent batches

blocks.content: 3. Pattern Two: the Work Queue Pattern
blocks.text: 3. Pattern Two: the Work Queue Pattern

blocks.content: A more advanced pattern sets only parallelism, with no fixed completions count, each Pod pulls work from a shared external queue and coordinates with the others itself, the Job simply keeps that many workers running until the queue is genuinely empty.

blocks.alt: Workers coordinating among themselves against a shared queue, no fixed count needed

blocks.content: Processing a large batch of independent items, resizing a few thousand images, for instance, is a natural fit for parallel Jobs, each item is independent, so running several workers concurrently finishes the whole batch meaningfully faster than one Pod working through it alone.

blocks.alt: Independent work items, finished meaningfully faster through real concurrency

blocks.content: A batch image-processing Job with completions: 100 and parallelism: 10 works through one hundred independent images, ten at a time, concurrently, rather than one at a time in sequence.

blocks.alt: One hundred items, worked through ten at a time, concurrently

blocks.content:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: image-resize
spec:
  completions: 100
  parallelism: 10
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: resizer
          image: image-resizer:1.0
      restartPolicy: OnFailure

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: parallelism lets several Job Pods run concurrently, either working toward a known completions total in batches, or pulling from a shared work queue with no fixed count.
This is the right tool for meaningfully speeding up a batch of independent work items, processing them concurrently instead of one at a time in sequence.
